body: Cc @CaselIT we may have to revert that change, I'm not sure how we missed this, that we are blending dataclass default with core default

right. that's a bit unfortunate.

Still it's strange that it breaks, since using the previous behavior the dataclass init would have set the `now` function on the instance, same as now, or I'm missing something? I mean the orm should see the same object in the instance, no?

OK on my computer now, let's stay that order

we have [insert_default](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/mapping_api.html#sqlalchemy.orm.mapped_column.params.insert_default) for this purpose, poster should use that.  

it's documented [here](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/dataclasses.html#column-defaults) in the docs
at the same time, let's adjust the new logic to see if "default" is already a callable

just note @RyogaWan we're going to add warnings for this, what you should do now is use the [insert_default](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/dataclasses.html#column-defaults) parameter instead of default

> 
I've tried and my code works fine. Many thanks!
for the record this regression is caused by the fix introduced in #9879

body:
**Federico Caselli** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**Fixed regression with callables as daclasses defaults** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4729

@RyogaWan , I’m using exactly the same technique for `created` and `updated` columns.
You can use standard data class’ `default_factory` parameter and provide callable here.

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

sqlalchemy==2.0.16 breaks default being function as described in this [guide](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/defaults.html).
I think [fix](https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4721/1/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/interfaces.py) for this [issue](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/9879) caused this regression.


### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.16

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

sqlite

### Database Vendor and Major Version

3.39.5

### Python Version

3.11

### Operating system

OSX

### To Reproduce

```python
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.orm import (DeclarativeBase, Mapped, MappedAsDataclass,
                            mapped_column, sessionmaker)

engine = sa.create_engine('sqlite:///:memory:', echo=True)
Session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
Session.configure(bind=engine)
session = Session()


class Base(DeclarativeBase, MappedAsDataclass):
    pass


def _context(context):
    event = context.get_current_parameters()['id']
    return str(event) + '_context'


class Test(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'test'

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    flag_df: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        default_factory=lambda: True,
        init=False,
    )
    flag_d: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(default=True, init=False)

    context_dependend_field: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        default=_context,
        init=False,
    )


Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

test = Test(id=uuid4())
session.add(test)
session.commit()
```
